STEP 2 - Ruler: the plate is square-ish with rounded corners, about 24 cm across. Its area is roughly 24 x 24 x 0.85 ≈ 490 cm^2. The apple is about 130 px wide and the plate about 345 px, so the apple is 24 x 130/345 ≈ 9 cm wide. That is a little large, so I assume about 8 cm.

STEP 3 - Items: one red-yellow apple, whole.

STEP 4 - Area: the apple covers about 50 cm^2 (π x 4^2), which is roughly 10% of the plate. The plate is otherwise empty.

STEP 5 - Volume: a sphere of 8 cm diameter has a volume of about 268 ml. Apples are slightly flattened, so I take about 250 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: apple density is about 0.8 g/ml, which gives about 200 g. A medium apple of 8 cm weighs 180-200 g, so I use 190 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: apple is about 52 kcal/100 g, so 190 g gives about 99 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: a single medium apple weighing about 190 g and giving about 100 kcal is plausible.
